author: NorthEast News Desk
body: American Eagle Outfitters shares fell sharply Thursday after the apparel retailer forecast flat gross margins for the current quarter and described continued weakness at its namesake brand.

The company kept its annual comparable-sales forecast unchanged after reporting second-quarter revenue above analysts’ expectations. Reuters said uneven discretionary spending and excess inventory have forced heavier promotions, particularly in women’s denim, putting pressure on profitability even as the Aerie intimates and activewear business remained stronger.

American Eagle has increased its investment in denim marketing to reach younger shoppers, but the core label continues to lose ground to competitors. Inventory costs were 14% higher from a year earlier, reflecting tariffs and other expenses, according to the report.

The share decline cited by Reuters occurred during Thursday’s trading and should not be read as a live price. The market reaction highlights investors’ concern that revenue resilience may not translate into stronger earnings while clearance activity remains elevated. American Eagle’s next results will show whether inventory reductions and new product campaigns can stabilize the flagship brand.
dek: The retailer kept its annual comparable-sales forecast after a revenue beat, but discounting and excess inventory continued to weigh on expectations.
headline: American Eagle shares slide on flat margin outlook and core-brand weakness
